justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: Customer Portal handles online submissions (R-01), Adjuster Workspace supports claims handlers (R-02), and the Claim-Type Feature Flag Evaluator alongside the Legacy Anti-Corruption Layer Adapter allows claim-by-claim migration (R-03).
justifications.performance_efficiency: CQRS pattern decouples adjuster views from 5-second mainframe latency: Read Model Projector asynchronously updates Adjuster Read Database (Cosmos DB), allowing Adjuster Workspace to achieve sub-2s response times via direct queries and point-reads.
justifications.compatibility: Integration & ACL Container, Mainframe Adapter, and IBM MQ enable seamless coexistence with the legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe, while Azure Active Directory integrates authentication. However, batch window coexistence mechanisms are not explicitly detailed.
justifications.usability: Both user groups are served by tailored frontends: Customer Portal provides a Claim Submission Wizard and Document Uploader for customers/brokers, while Adjuster Workspace provides an optimized UI for internal claims adjusters.
justifications.reliability: IBM MQ guarantees message delivery, Event Consumer Component enforces idempotency to prevent duplicate processing, and Rate Limiter & Circuit Breaker protects the fragile legacy mainframe. End-to-end failure compensation across hybrid boundaries has minor gaps.
justifications.security: Meets R-07 thoroughly via Azure Active Directory integration using OAuth 2.0/PKCE in frontends, token validation in API Gateway, mTLS for IBM MQ mainframe communication, and Private Endpoints for Adjuster Read Database.
justifications.maintainability: Claim-Type Feature Flag Evaluator and Dynamic Route Orchestrator enable sub-day rollback to the mainframe (R-06). Modularity is strong with Anti-Corruption Layer isolation, clear CQRS boundaries, and domain-driven design in Claims Core Container.
justifications.portability: Architecture respects the hybrid deployment model using IBM MQ across on-premises mainframe and Azure West Europe. However, tight coupling to proprietary Azure PaaS services (Cosmos DB, APIM policies) limits cloud-provider portability.

PERF-01.justification: Adjuster screens read denormalized projections directly from Azure Cosmos DB via CQRS, completely decoupling frontend response times from slow mainframe backend latencies.
sensitivity_points: Projection latency from IBM MQ to Cosmos DB
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency for adjuster screens versus immediate read latency

PERF-02.justification: Peak online submissions are buffered asynchronously through API Gateway and IBM MQ message queues, preventing submission spikes from spilling over into the mainframe nightly batch window.
sensitivity_points: Queue buffer capacity in IBM MQ during month-end peaks
tradeoffs: Asynchronous processing complexity versus protection of the mainframe batch window

AVAIL-01.justification: Claims intake remains operational during mainframe downtime because submissions are persisted in Azure SQL and IBM MQ message queues, then forwarded once the batch window closes.
sensitivity_points: Message queue persistence and retention during mainframe downtime
tradeoffs: Delayed mainframe synchronization versus continuous portal availability

AVAIL-02.justification: IBM MQ persistent messaging and checkpoint idempotency filters prevent message loss and duplicate processing, although detailed end-to-end transactional compensation across the mainframe boundary is lightly specified.
sensitivity_points: Idempotency key enforcement across hybrid cloud-mainframe transactions
tradeoffs: Guaranteed deduplication overhead versus sync throughput

MOD-01.justification: The API Gateway features a Claim-Type Feature Flag Evaluator that dynamically steers traffic between legacy and modern workflows, allowing one-day rollback without mainframe modifications.
sensitivity_points: Centralized feature flag evaluation latency in API Management
tradeoffs: Routing rule complexity in API Gateway versus ease of rollback

MOD-02.justification: User interfaces interact only with the modern API Gateway and Cosmos DB, while the Anti-Corruption Layer isolates legacy protocols. Retiring the mainframe requires zero UI changes.
sensitivity_points: Strict adherence to domain boundaries within the Anti-Corruption Layer
tradeoffs: Layered abstraction maintenance cost versus simplified legacy decommissioning

SEC-01.justification: Azure Active Directory and API Gateway enforce JWT validation and RBAC, but fine-grained broker-to-customer claim isolation logic relies on backend domain enforcement rather than gateway policies.
sensitivity_points: Granular tenant-level claim authorization checks in core domain services
tradeoffs: Centralized gateway authentication versus distributed domain authorization logic

SEC-02.justification: Revoking accounts in Azure Active Directory stops new sessions via SSO, but revoking existing Cosmos DB ephemeral resource tokens and legacy mainframe sessions within 15 minutes is not addressed.
sensitivity_points: Lifespan of active JWTs and ephemeral Cosmos DB resource tokens
tradeoffs: Fast UI query performance using direct tokens versus immediate access revocation
